name: Nekoda
title: Ancestor of temple workers who returned from exile
summary: Nekoda is mentioned in the biblical lists of those who returned from the Babylonian exile. The name appears in two contexts: as an ancestor of a group of temple servants (netinim), and as an ancestor of a group that could not prove their Israelite origin. Nekoda is a lesser-known figure but represents the many unnamed families who participated in rebuilding Israel's community after the exile.

keyEvents.title: Descendants of Nekoda in the list of temple servants
keyEvents.description: The descendants of Nekoda are listed among the temple servants (netinim) who returned from Babylon to Jerusalem with Zerubbabel.

keyEvents.title: Repetition in Nehemiah's list of temple servants
keyEvents.description: Nekoda's family is mentioned again in the parallel list in the book of Nehemiah among the temple servants who returned.

keyEvents.title: Another Nekoda – without proven lineage
keyEvents.description: Another group called the descendants of Nekoda could not prove that they belonged to Israel and are listed among those with uncertain origin.

keyEvents.title: Parallel list of those without proven lineage in Nehemiah
keyEvents.description: The same group of uncertain origin, including the descendants of Nekoda, is mentioned in Nehemiah's parallel list.

keyEvents.title: The Return from the Babylonian Exile
keyEvents.description: Nekoda's family was part of the great return under Zerubbabel's leadership, where thousands of Jews returned to rebuild the temple and Jerusalem.
